status.summary: The City of Columbus Department of Building and Zoning Services permit layer (data version of 26 October 2026) records commercial structural alteration permit ALTC2502418 for '225 RATHMELL RD UNIT CLB4' on parcel 510180711 (288,000 sq ft; valuation 110,000,000 USD; issued 1 May 2025) with status 'Final Inspection Approved' and application status 'Closed' as of 6 October 2026. CLB4's electrical, mechanical, plumbing and fire-suppression permits had already been finaled between 6 May and 23 July 2026. This government record establishes that the permitted CLB4 alteration works were completed and passed final inspection on 6 October 2026. Completion is limited to that alteration permit: the building's new-structure permit (NEWC2430776) is still shown as issued, and no certificate of occupancy, opening, operation, IT load or tenant is established. Other campus works (CLB3, two 52,500 sq ft structures, a 300,000 sq ft alteration and an office building) are not part of this project.

locator.identity_review: Every CLB4 permit, and all 140 permits returned for parcel 510180711, are at 225 Rathmell Rd. The Franklin County Auditor record for 510-180711 has site address 225 Rathmell Rd, owner Magellan Enterprises LLC, tax mailing name Google LLC and land-use class 375 'data center'; of the county's 18 class-375 parcels it is the only one whose tax mailing name is Google LLC. Columbus Ordinance 0520-2021 (passed 25 March 2021) describes Magellan Enterprises LLC's proposal to develop, construct and operate one or more data centers, with accessory offices and utility buildings, on 495.9 acres at 5076 South High Street, parcel 510-180711. Google's Ohio page lists Columbus among its Ohio data-center communities. The City's permit-layer points for CLB4 fall inside the parcel but are inconsistent between permits, so the parcel centroid is used. No geocoder, map viewport or city centre is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The county publishes no positional accuracy for parcel polygons; the centroid represents a 480-acre campus parcel about 1.2 by 2.2 km, and the position of building CLB4 within it is not published.

status.summary: The City of Farmington's project page for the Farmington Technology Park Project (developer Tract), in its update dated 16 September 2026, reports that the plaintiffs in both legal matters involving the City (litigation that had asked the court to stop steps in the development process) have filed dismissals that await final directions from the court. The page records the City's 2024 approvals for the data-center technology park (final AUAR, comprehensive-plan amendment, rezoning, preliminary and final plat, PUD-1 Ordinance 2024-12 and a development contract), the April 2026 division of the plat into a 1st Addition (former Fountain Valley Golf Course) and a 2nd Addition with updated development contracts, and recording of the 1st Addition plat on 19 May 2026. The PUD leaves site, grading and building plans to later City approval, and no site plan, building permit or data-centre construction is recorded, so the campus is recorded as announced on 16 September 2026. The demolition of former golf-course buildings (permit issued 18 May, finaled 30 June 2026) predates the window and is not treated as data-centre construction.
